text: May 6 is inextricably linked to our respect and gratitude toward the invincible Bulgarian armed forces, said Patriarch Daniil (06.05.2026 10:54)

In the tradition of Bulgarian statehood and church life, May 6 is inseparably linked to our reverence and gratitude toward the invincible Bulgarian armed forces. This was said by Bulgarian Patriarch and Metropolitan of Sofia Daniil, who today led the solemn blessing service with the consecration of the battle flags in the capital.

“In an unchanging witness to the triumph of life, which came with the Resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, I wholeheartedly greet you on the most radiant feast of the holy and glorious Great Martyr George — a wondrous warrior of Christ in faith and virtues, and our universally glorified heavenly intercessor and miracle-worker. Following the tradition of May 6, on the festive day of Saint George the Victorious, our Holy Orthodox Church consecrates the banners of the battle glory of our victorious Army, imploring God’s mercy and protection for our Orthodox soldiery, which preserves the peace and security of our dear homeland and, with a sense of duty, watches over the life and honor of Bulgarian citizens,” Patriarch Daniil added.

According to him, “our prayers and the sacred rites appointed for today’s festive day are grounded in the historically attested truth that, throughout our age-old Orthodox tradition, the trust of the Bulgarian armed forces has always been first and foremost in God — in Him from whom we know that all true strength and power come, as well as in our faith in Christ the Savior, which has been the guiding conviction not only of the Christian warrior and martyr Saint George, celebrated today by the Holy Church, but also of all Bulgarian warriors who entered battle in defense of their brothers and sisters in faith and kin.”

“The sources for the thousand-year history of our people tell us that the tradition of the consecration of battle flags dates back to the First Bulgarian Empire, to the time of the glorious Bulgarian Tsar Simeon I the Great. The first such historically attested event was the consecration carried out in 917 — before the battle at the Achelous River, victorious for Bulgarian arms. In the performance of this ritual, the power of our great ancestors’ trust in God and His eternal righteousness is revealed to us; their conviction that without God and the grace-filled power that comes from Him to human beings, we cannot do anything that is truly good and beneficial. Our Lord Jesus Christ tells us the same: ‘… he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing,’” Patriarch Daniel recalled.

“Guided by this faith and this conviction, our great ancestors throughout the ages have sought and implored God’s help in every undertaking of theirs. This is what we are doing today as well, when, in unity and harmony between Church and state, we beseech God’s help for our glorious armed forces, peace, light, and prosperity for our people and our Homeland. May the sprinkling of these battle banners with water sanctified through God’s grace be yet another testimony to our faith in God and a visible sign of God’s favor and God’s protection over our entire people and especially over the Bulgarian servicemen who have devoted their lives to the sacrificial military service in the ranks of the Bulgarian Army,” said the Bulgarian patriarch.
